title: Multimodal caption noise probe
content:
Context and motivation: This is a freeform scratchpad for thinking through noisy caption / alt-text / surrounding text that comes with images in our multimodal ingest. Most of our downstream tasks (caption-to-embedding, caption-to-ranking, caption-conditioned generation) assume a reasonable natural-language caption. But in reality captions are: filenames, OCR text, HTML breadcrumbs, watermarks, timestamps, mixed languages, emojis, bot-generated gibberish, or long technical logs. We need lightweight annotation heuristics + a small cleanup pipeline so model quality doesn't degrade on real-world inputs. High-level goals: - Define simple label classes that are cheap to annotate and useful for automatic filters. - Provide deterministic normalization rules (regex-first) with an escape hatch for human review. - Prioritize fixes that have high downstream ROI: remove filenames, strip HTML, collapse OCR line breaks, preserve semantic emojis, flag PII. Proposed label taxonomy (single-choice primary + multi-label flags): - primary_label: clean | noise:ocr | noise:filename | noise:watermark | noise:html | noise:bot | noise:translation-artifact | noise:lang-mismatch | noise:log | missing - flags (multi): contains-emoji, contains-url, contains-email, contains-phone, has-non-latin-script, likely-ocr-linebreaks, likely-watermark, filename-derived Annotation UI guidance (short): - Show image + original caption (native text) + a small preview of OCR overlay if available. - Primary label: pick the single most actionable problem. If multiple apply, pick the one that will cause the worst model failure (e.g., filename > stray punctuation). - Normalized caption: annotator should write the cleaned-up caption (1–2 sentences) if primary_label != clean. Keep original in the metadata. - If caption is obviously auto-generated (e.g., "Image may contain: ..." or "Stock photo - ...") tag as noise:bot and add note. - PII: if caption contains email/phone/address, tag contains-email/phone and escalate (PII workflow). Heuristics / deterministic rules to try before human label: (pipeline order matters) 1) HTML strip: remove tags, decode entities. If >50% tag content removed, mark noise:html. 2) Filename detection: heuristic if caption matches regex like ^[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{3,}\.jpg|png|jpeg|gif$ OR contains camera model tokens (IMG_, DSC, PXL). - If true, set primary_label=noise:filename and normalized_caption="" (or use OCR if present). 3) OCR collapse: if caption contains many linebreaks ( ) and avg line length < 40, replace linebreaks with spaces, fix hyphenation. Flag likely-ocr-linebreaks. 4) Watermark/credit stripping: common patterns (©, Copyright, / by / Photo by) -> remove from normalized caption and set flag likely-watermark. 5) Long numeric strings: if caption is predominantly digits + punctuation ( > 70% numeric chars ) -> noise:log or filename depending on separators. 6) Language detection mismatch: detect language of caption and of surrounding metadata; if mismatch and caption is very short (<5 tokens), mark noise:lang-mismatch. 7) Emoji handling: preserve emojis as tokens; add contains-emoji flag. 8) Bot/generated wrappers: patterns like "AI generated description", "Alt text: None" -> noise:bot. Concrete examples (realistic-ish): - "IMG_20240202_174512.jpg" -> primary_label: noise:filename; normalized_caption: ""; notes: use OCR if present. - "Sunset over bay -- HDR (edited)" -> primary_label: clean (or noise:bot if contains "(edited)" frequently causing garbage). Normalized_caption: "Sunset over the bay." - "
Read more at example.com
" -> primary_label: noise:html; normalized_caption: "" or if surrounding text present, extract sentence content. - "P©J. SMITH" -> primary_label: noise:watermark; normalized_caption: ""; flag: likely-watermark. - "Ckeck-out the new iPhon!!!" -> primary_label: clean? or noise:bot/typo? Proposed: treat as clean (model can handle typos) unless typos exceed threshold (>=3 edits to reasonable token). - "12:34:56 2023-10-11 ERROR: ..." -> primary_label: noise:log; normalized_caption: ""; flag: noise:log. Sampling strategy for small human review set (1000 samples): - 300 random captions (baseline) - 200 high-punctuation ratio (>40%) - 200 low-alpha ratio (<30% letters) - 150 mismatch language detection vs. metadata - 150 filenames/IMG_ tokens (filename heuristics) This should help estimate prevalence of each noise type and surface rare cases. Downstream rules (fast filters used in model pipeline): - If primary_label in {noise:filename, noise:log, noise:bot} -> drop caption from model input (use empty string) unless OCR returns a reasonable sentence. - If noise:html -> attempt HTML extraction and re-run normalization; if nothing left, drop. - If contains-PII flags -> route to redaction step before passing to model. - For embeddings: if normalized_caption is empty and image has reliable OCR, use OCR text (post-cleaning) as caption. Annotation examples with edge fuzziness (for training annotators): 1) "iphone_14_pro_front_0001.png" -> noise:filename (clear) 2) "The quick brown fox jumps..." (with file name appended) -> primary_label: clean; normalized_caption: sentence only; strip filename. 3) "عائله سعيد" (Arabic name) when metadata language is English short caption -> flag likely-lang-mismatch (but likely clean). 4) "😂😂😂" -> primary_label: clean? or noise:bot? Proposal: treat as clean but add contains-emoji flag; only escalate if caption is solely punctuation/emoji and no semantic content and task needs text. Annotation form fields (short schema): - original_caption (stored) - primary_label (one of taxonomy) - flags (list) - normalized_caption (string) - keep_original_boolean (Y/N) - normalization_notes (free text, optional) Edge rules / gotchas: - Filenames that are also good text: "bridge_view_2021" -> ambiguous; prioritize human review if downstream confidence drops. - Mixed-language: prefer the longer-language segment. - Captions with embedded alt text markup (e.g., "[caption]text[/caption]") -> strip tags but preserve inner. - Large blobs from scraped pages (long footers) -> consider truncation to first 30 tokens after HTML strip. Evaluation metrics to track post-cleanup: - % captions dropped or replaced by OCR - distribution of primary_label across dataset - downstream embedding cosine drift on a small benchmark (should improve after cleaning) - model perplexity on cleaned vs original captions (for generation tasks) Short-term action items (me + collaborators): - [ ] Kick off 1k-sample job (Diego) with priority sampling queries above (JIRA-ML-4829). - [ ] Prototype regex-based filename detector and HTML stripper (Samir) and run on a 100k preview. - [ ] Draft a 1-page annotator cheat-sheet with examples (Maya). - [ ] Add unit tests for heuristics and edgecases in datasets repo (PR referenced above). Open questions / discussion points: - Do we want to normalize obvious typos or leave them for model robustness? My bias: normalize extreme typos that are tokenization-breaking, but leave small misspellings. - For short captions (<=3 tokens) with language mismatch, should we keep or drop? This affects recall for named entities. - Should we collapse repeated emoji strings into a single token? (e.g. 😂😂😂 -> 😂) Notes to self: - When writing cheat-sheet, include dozens of tiny examples (filenames + overlay + watermark + logs) — annotators learn by seeing near-miss cases. - Check with privacy team about whether filenames ever contain user ids; if so, treat as PII and escalate. Slack refs / links to follow-up threads: - slack: #datasets -> thread "caption-cleanup-strategy" (search: caption-cleanup 2025-07) End of scratchpad. (If this is useful, convert to a short confluence page with examples and a checklist for reviewers.)
